cases.focus: Identify the four harmonies and their basses; does the final cadence meet the strict soprano-and-bass condition for a perfect authentic cadence?

Final V-I has D3-G2 in bass and A4-G4 in soprano: root-position dominant and tonic, soprano ends on tonic; PAC in this schematic metrical context.

cases.focus: Explain the event across measures 4-5, identify the harmony and inversion in measures 5-7, and give one student revision suggestion without treating every vertical slice as a new functional chord.

checks.expected: C5 is prepared in m4, tied over G bass on beat1 m5, resolves downward to B4 on beat2: 4-3 suspension.

cases.focus: Give a basic harmonic and phrase overview. Identify any applied dominant and resolution, inversions in measures 3 and 7, the sonority in measure 11, and whether G-sharp from measure 5 affects measure 13. Distinguish score facts from tentative formal or aesthetic judgments.

m3 C/E first inversion; m7 Dm/F first inversion.

system: You are a careful music tutor helping a student revise a short score. Analyze only the supplied notation. Be concrete about measure numbers, pitches and bass. Separate literal sonorities, harmonic interpretation, and aesthetic judgment. Computed root/quality guesses may be wrong around non-chord tones. Respond in at most 400 words. Do not invent missing information.
protocol: Three independent paired calls, all baselines frozen before computing evidence. Same model/settings/base messages. Evidence arm receives fixed real music21 results as an additional user message. This tests supplied evidence, not autonomous tool selection. Checks are author-generated, reviewable expectations; not an external gold dataset.
